 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Utah Utes offensive tackle Kelvin Obot is out for the season with a lower leg injury, head coach Morgan Scalley said this week.
 "By way of an announcement on the injury front, Kelvin Obot is out for the season," Scalley said. "Lower leg deal. Not getting into the specifics there, but he'll be done for the year."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Obot left Utah's win over Colorado on Oct. 17 during a run play. The rare freshman starter was expected to make a huge difference for the Utes in their potential Playoff run. He was put ahead of Cedric Jefferson and Keith Olson midway through the season.
 Every year in college football there seems to be a true freshman that sticks out above the rest. Whether that was Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin picking up a huge victory over Texas or Malachi Toney being the difference maker in Miami's national championship run.
 Because of the NIL era, the chances a freshman will play an expanded role or even start at a key position have skyrocketed. Remember, college football wasn't always like that. There was a time when underclassmen rarely played. And starting wasn't considered unless there were injuries. That meant burning a possible redshirt to see action in a game. Times have evolved, and the game has become more accepting of players being instant contributors.
 If a player is a generational talent, he won't last long due to NFL dreams. Three years and out in most cases around the country. Obot was named ESPN's No. 1 freshman to make an impact in the Big 12 conference before the season.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement After losing the entire starting five in the trenches, Obot was in the rotation for the Utes and relied upon heavily. Utah had two offensive linemen taken in the first round in the 2026 NFL Draft. Without Spencer Fano and Caleb Lomu, Obot was the next group of leaders trying to establish himself in Salt Lake City.
 Utes offensive line coach Jordan Gross has been key to Obot's development. The former NFL All-Pro has been able to take the former five-star talent into the next phase of his career. There aren't many former players who have reached the same heights as Gross and went into coaching.
 Obot has all the skills to be great. At 6-foot-5 and 300 pounds, the Idaho Player of the Year played in the trenches as a two-way star last season for Fruitland. He was on an offense that averaged 42.2 points and 448.4 yards per game. Obot also racked up 75 tackles (27 TFL) and 8.5 sacks. Being able to fully understand the positions on the other side of the line will be helpful for him at Utah. He's a blue-chip talent who will be a force for many years to come.
 Obot being unavailable will be a significant blow for No. 3 Utah as they'll face a 'Holy War' battle with No. 7 BYU on Saturday ( Noon ET, ABC ).
